items.title: Microsoft & Snowflake’s Commitment to Apache Ossie
items.excerpt: If you haven't already, check out FabCon and SQLCon 2026 in Barcelona: Building the data foundation for Microsoft Copilot and Agents for a complete look at all of our FabCon Europe announcements across Fabric and Microsoft Databases. Advancing an open, interoperable semantic foundation for AI-powered analytics Today, Microsoft is pleased to affirm our commitment to Apache Ossie (incubating) , a community-led effort to establish a vendor-neutral standard for exchanging semantic metadata across analytics, AI, and BI platforms. This has been a close collaboration with Snowflake, who helped found Ossie . We have heard loud and clear that customers want to enable platform-agnostic agentic experiences. Shared semantic context must be defined once and reused across platforms, enabling agentic consumption at scale, maximizing the reach of AI-powered analytics, and empowering users to leverage the best agent for the job. Power BI semantic models are key enablers of AI-powered analysis, providing humans and AI agents with governed semantic context to answer data questions quickly and confidently. items.title: What Databricks is doing with Genie for Business Users
items.excerpt: I n a little o ver two years, Genie has gone from a Public Preview feature for asking questions of your data in plain English, to the main way Databricks wants business users to work with the platform. September's releases show where it's going next: the Excel Add-in and the Genie One MCP server both went GA, and at the end of the month Databricks bought Row Zero, a spreadsheet company, to build into Genie.

items.title: DataFrame caching on serverless compute is now in Public Preview
items.excerpt: DataFrame caching on serverless compute is now in Public Preview . You can cache a DataFrame with df.cache() or df.persist() on serverless compute to reuse an expensive result for the rest of your session. Caching requires serverless environment version 5 or above, Databricks Connect for Python 18.1.8 or above, or Databricks Connect for Scala 18.1.5 or above. The preview is enabled by default for most workspaces. Workspace admins can disable it from the Previews page. See Cache DataFrames on serverless compute .

items.title: Genie One enhancements
items.excerpt: Conversation outline : Use the conversation outline along the left edge of Genie One conversations to jump between your messages. Hover over a tick in the outline to preview a message and the start of its response. See Navigate a long conversation . Upload skills (Public Preview) : You can now click Upload skills to upload your existing skill files and folders to your skills folder in the workspace. See Upload a skill . Snippets from external tool queries (Public Preview) : Genie Ontology now also extracts snippets from queries that external tools , such as dbt, run on Azure Databricks. These runs appear in query history alongside queries that you run in Azure Databricks. See Genie Ontology . Remembered sign-in email in the Genie mobile app (Public Preview) : The Genie mobile app now remembers the email address of the last user who signed in and prefills it at the next sign-in. See Use Genie on mobile .
